subject: Re: Kickoff: CamP Zip-NeRF - staffing, compute, and the synthetic-data pipeline
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Milan 60% (TL, owns the JAX pipeline incl. the pycolmap quirk - the README is explicit that pip's pycolmap is the wrong one, so that goes in the setup doc in bold). Yusuf 40% on the CamP perturbed-pose ablations. Katya 60% - see below.

Compute: Zip-NeRF training is heavy; the release's own scripts warn the full reproduction takes a long time. Estimate: ~110 A100-days for both dataset repros plus the CamP ablation grid. titan-a100 best-effort should absorb that spread over six weeks; if contention bites in March I'll ask Ines for a short vulcan slice.

On eval data: the public benchmarks won't answer the capture-robustness question - we need scenes where we control pose error and scene content exactly. Nothing exists in-house for this, so we're scoping and staffing a synthetic-data generation pipeline built from scratch - Katya owns it at 60%: procedurally generated scenes, randomized camera trajectories, and rendered ground truth we control end to end. First usable scenes by Mar 20 to feed the M2 ablations.

Deshawn
